title: ralph loop: sandbox-exec profile too restrictive — Claude exits instantly
description:
Commit d8a5ac3 (#211) introduced container-first execution via macOS sandbox-exec. The sandbox profile uses (deny default) and only grants write access to the worktree and .ralph dir. But Claude CLI needs write access to ~/.claude/ for session state, and possibly ~/Library/ for temp files. Claude starts, gets denied on its first write, and exits immediately with no completion signal. Every iteration fails in 0 seconds.

Fix: disable sandboxing by default until the profile is validated. The safest immediate fix is to gate it behind a --sandbox flag rather than auto-enabling when sandbox-exec is present.

Introduced in: d8a5ac3 feat: centralized agent module with container-first execution (#211)

title: Resume with uncommitted changes should stash, rebase, then reapply
description: When ralph is Ctrl-C'd mid-task and resumed, uncommitted changes in the worktree prevent rebase onto latest main. The worktree stays stale, missing any direct pushes. On resume: stash uncommitted changes, rebase onto origin/main, stash pop. If stash pop conflicts, commit the stash as a WIP commit and let the agent resolve on its next iteration.
close_reason: stash/rebase/pop on resume — commit b5a42ff

title: Include full bead context in agent task prompt: notes, comments, labels, dependencies
description: The agent only receives the bead title and description. In bash mode, the full plan with detailed context was visible. With beads, notes, comments, labels, and dependencies are missing — the agent has to run bd show itself (which it often skips). The orchestrator should fetch and inject the complete bead context into the task prompt. This explains why agents have been struggling more since the Go migration.
close_reason: completed by ralph — PR #159

title: Skip task after repeated LLM rejections instead of fail-open or looping
description: After the fix agent runs and LLM still rejects, the current behavior is fail-open (accept anyway). This lets incomplete work through. Fail-closed would loop forever. The third option: skip the task — mark it as blocked with the LLM rejection reason, move to the next task. The attempt history preserves the feedback so the next pickup knows what didn't work. Replaces the current fail-open at loop.go line ~427.
close_reason: implemented: Haiku → fix agent → Sonnet escalation → skip on double reject — commit d7beab2

title: VerifyDir should be worktree, not project directory
description: The orchestrator runs post-signal tests with VerifyDir set to cfg.ProjectDir (main repo), not the worktree where the agent made changes. Tests run against the project directory code, not the agent's code. This causes false failures when the project directory has different test expectations than the worktree, and false passes when the agent breaks something that the project directory doesn't test.
close_reason: fixed: VerifyDir = gm.WorkDir — commit f9440e2

title: Squash-merge overwrites direct pushes to base branch
description: When we push fixes directly to develop/main while ralph is mid-task, ralph's branch (forked before the fix) doesn't have the fix. When ralph squash-merges its PR, our fix gets overwritten. Root causes: (1) rebase only happens at iteration start, not before push, (2) if rebase was broken (origin/develop issue), branches never pick up base branch changes. Fix: rebase onto base branch before pushing, not just at iteration start. This is the #1 source of recurring regressions.
close_reason: completed by ralph — PR #147

title: Task not closed after successful merge — same task reloaded next iteration
description: After the agent completes work, verification passes, and the PR is merged, ralph picks up the same task on the next iteration. CloseTask runs at line 539 before pushAndCreatePR, so either CloseTask is failing silently or GetNextTaskInfo is returning closed tasks. This causes infinite loops on already-completed work.
close_reason: fixed: removed silent status pre-check in CloseTask (commit 11a17cf)

title: [bug] Rebase conflicts still occur on resume despite force-reset fix
description: ralph-c7b and ralph-2y8 were closed as fixed but rebase conflicts still happen on every resume. The force-reset after merge works within a run but the worktree reverts to a stale branch after evolve restart or stop/resume. The worktree branch stored in state.json may point to a branch that was deleted after squash-merge. On resume, ralph tries to rebase this stale branch instead of starting fresh from origin/main. Fix: on resume, always verify the worktree branch still exists and is based on latest origin/main. If not, silently recreate from main without prompting.
close_reason: completed by ralph

title: LLM verification should check code state, not just iteration diff
description: When work was already merged in a previous iteration but the bead is still open, the iteration diff is empty/trivial. The LLM rejects because it only sees the small diff, not the full implementation. Fix: when there are no new commits (warning), the LLM should verify the CURRENT code state against the bead requirements, not just the iteration diff. Pass the relevant source files instead of the diff. 'Is this feature already implemented in the codebase?'
close_reason: completed by ralph

title: [bug] Evolve exec doesn't replace process — old ralph keeps running
description: killChildProcesses uses 'pkill -P' which kills ALL child processes including Go runtime threads. This corrupts the Go runtime, making syscall.Exec fail or behave unpredictably — the old process continues running alongside the new one. Fix: don't use pkill -P. Instead, track specific tail and stream-filter PIDs in the runner and kill only those before exec. The Go runtime's threads must not be touched.
close_reason: Root cause was pkill -P killing Go runtime threads. Removed killChildProcesses. Duplicate output is from goroutine accumulation (ralph-t47), not zombie processes.

title: [bug] SessionName test depends on live tmux state
description: TestSessionName_BasenameLoop fails when a tabi-loop tmux session is actually running on the machine. The test checks SessionName() which appends -2 if the session name collides with an existing tmux session. Unit tests must not depend on live system state. Fix: mock the tmux session check (sessionExists) so the test is deterministic regardless of what's running.
notes: Any test that depends on or affects system state outside the worktree is a P0. This test queries live tmux sessions. Other tests might affect git config, create files outside the worktree, etc. All tests must be pure — no side effects, no system state dependencies. Containers would fix this but tests should be correct regardless.
close_reason: Fixed: sessionExists is now a var stubbed in tests. TestSessionName_BasenameLoop no longer queries live tmux. All tests pass.

title: Orchestrator verification: keep agent alive, retry on test failure
description: Signal means 'verify me' not 'kill me'. Agent stays alive after signaling. Orchestrator syncs prompts and runs full test suite. If tests fail → write failure output to feedback file → agent reads it, fixes, signals again → repeat until green. If tests pass → agent proceeds with git commit/push/PR. Orchestrator closes bead after merge. Agent is only killed after successful completion.
close_reason: Implemented: OnSignal callback in claude runner. Agent stays alive after signaling. Orchestrator syncs prompts, runs tests. If fail → clears signal, writes feedback, agent continues. If pass → agent killed. Falls back to legacy verification for test stubs. All tests pass.

title: Restructure repo: move bash to bash/, prompts into go/, go/ becomes root
description: Final cleanup once Go is the primary: (1) move bash code (ralph.sh, lib/, test/) into a bash/ archive folder, (2) move prompts/ into go/ so they're co-located with the embed directive — no more copy step, (3) make go/ the repo root (move go/* to top level, remove go/ nesting). This eliminates: the prompts sync issue, the rebuild-go.sh copy step, the go/cmd/ralph/prompts gitignore, and the 'run from go/' confusion. The Go module becomes the repo.
close_reason: prompts moved to go/cmd/ralph/prompts as tracked source — commit 7ecf2d1

title: Orchestrator runs rebuild-go.sh before test verification
description: When the agent signals completion, the orchestrator must run scripts/rebuild-go.sh BEFORE running the test suite. The agent may have modified prompts/ or go/ files — without rebuilding, the embedded prompts sync test always fails, causing infinite retry loops. Sequence: agent signals → orchestrator rebuilds → orchestrator runs tests → pass/fail decision.
close_reason: Fixed: orchestrator now syncs prompts from worktree's prompts/ to go/cmd/ralph/prompts/ before running test verification. Committed on main.

title: [bug] Beads log lines appear duplicated from orchestrator
description: After fixing tail process leaks (ralph-t47), [beads] log lines still appear duplicated. Only 2 tail processes running (correct). The duplication is in the orchestrator — it logs the same event twice, likely reading the signal file and then processing it separately. Not a tail/stream issue. Check where [beads] messages are emitted in the loop and signal handling code.
close_reason: completed by ralph — PR #144

title: Orchestrator runs full test suite as sole verification gate
description:
Two phases — must be done in order:

PHASE 1: Keep agent alive for retry loop.
Agent signals 'verify me' → orchestrator syncs prompts, runs tests → if fail, write failure to feedback file, agent reads and fixes → repeat until green. Agent still does git commit/push/PR for now. Once tests pass, agent signals final completion, orchestrator closes bead.

PHASE 2 (separate bead): Move git workflow to orchestrator.
After phase 1 is stable, move commit/push/PR/merge from agent to orchestrator. Then lock agent out of git/gh/bd. This is a bigger change — create a new bead for it when ready.

Current phase 1 focus: signal means 'verify me' not 'kill me'. Agent stays alive. Orchestrator runs tests. Retry on failure.
notes:
Current behavior: verification fails → logs warning → continues to NEXT task. Should: verification fails → spawn new Claude on SAME task with test failure output in prompt → repeat until tests pass. The agent is dead after signaling — orchestrator must spawn a new one for retry. The retry prompt includes: original task, what was attempted (from attempt tracker), and the test failure output.
After tests pass, the ORCHESTRATOR handles: commit, push, create PR, squash-merge, close bead, force-reset. The agent never runs git push, gh pr create, or bd close. The agent's scope ends at writing code and signaling. This also means removing git push and gh pr create from the agent's prompt instructions.
Lock down agent tools further: remove git, gh, and bd from allowed commands entirely. The agent only needs: file read/write/edit, project build/test commands (go, npm, make, etc.), and grep/glob for code search. The orchestrator passes task context via the prompt (bead description, test state, reflections, attempt history). The agent has zero access to git, GitHub, or beads. Disallowed: Bash(git*), Bash(gh*), Bash(bd*).
close_reason: Splitting into two beads with proper dependency chain

title: [bug] Changes from worktree leak onto main via shared .git
description: Changes from worktree leak onto main's index on every stop/resume cycle. Happens on both ralph and tabi — not evolve-specific. After ralph stop + resume, main has staged changes that would revert the latest merged PRs. The ff-only evolve fix didn't help because the contamination happens during normal operation, likely during: (1) RecreateFromMain (fresh worktree from option 1), (2) PostMergeReset force-checkout, (3) rebase operations, or (4) worktree cleanup on exit. Root cause unknown — git worktrees should have separate indexes. Need to investigate whether the worktree .git file is intact or if something is breaking the worktree linkage.
notes:
Confirmed dangerous: force-reset in worktree stages REVERSIONS of merged PRs on main's index. If accidentally committed, it would revert the latest PR. This happened with PR #118 — 361 deletions staged on main that would have undone the orchestrator-owns-close work. The shared .git directory means any index-modifying operation in the worktree affects main.
PR #124 added reset --hard HEAD after update-ref in postMergeUpdate. Still contaminating. The update-ref path may not be the culprit — likely PostMergeReset's 'git checkout --force -B' in the worktree is the real cause. Need to add logging to identify exactly which git operation causes the index change on main. Approach: run 'git status --porcelain' on projectDir before and after each git operation in PostMergeReset and postMergeUpdate to isolate the exact line.
close_reason: completed by ralph

title: Ralph repo needs required CI status checks
description: Ralph's GitHub repo has no required status checks on main branch. PRs merge even when CI is red. This lets ralph merge broken code via auto-merge. Add a required 'test' status check to the ralph repo's branch protection, same as tabi. This is prerequisite for ralph-tu5 (CI-gated repos) — ralph itself needs to be CI-gated first.
close_reason: The real fix is ralph-4tt — orchestrator runs tests locally before push. CI gate is a backup, not the primary gate. Repo protection still enabled but shouldn't be needed once orchestrator verification works.

title: Orchestrator: LLM verification — does the diff match the bead?
description: After tests pass in the OnSignal callback, before accepting the signal: (1) get the git diff of the agent's changes, (2) get the bead description/acceptance criteria, (3) call Claude Haiku with a minimal prompt: 'Does this diff implement what the bead asks for? Do the tests prove the functionality? Answer YES or NO with one-line reasoning.' (4) If NO → write reasoning to feedback file, clear signal, agent retries. (5) If YES → accept signal, proceed to close/merge. Uses Haiku for speed/cost. The prompt includes: diff, bead title+description, test file changes. This catches: tests that assert true, fixes that don't match the bead, missing functionality.
close_reason: Implemented: LLMVerifyDiff in verify package calls Claude Haiku with diff + bead description. Wired into OnSignal callback after tests pass. If rejected, writes feedback and agent retries. All tests pass.

title: [bug] Agent closes beads it's not assigned to
description: The agent modifies beads it's not assigned to — closing, updating, or otherwise interfering with beads outside its current task. This is separate from ralph-4tt (orchestrator owns close). Even after ralph-4tt, the agent could still update/reopen/comment on other beads. Fix: the execution prompt must explicitly state 'ONLY interact with bead {ID} — do not read, update, close, or modify any other bead. bd prime is read-only context, not an invitation to manage other issues.'
notes: Agent is writing tests with 'verifyFunc that always passes' — this proves nothing. Tests must exercise real failure paths: what happens when verification fails? Does the bead stay open? Does the agent retry? A test that only covers the happy path with stubbed-out verification is exactly the problem we're trying to solve.
close_reason: Moved task closing from agent to orchestrator. Agent prompt no longer instructs bd close; the loop calls CloseTask after verification. PR #117.

title: [bug] Go tests launch full ralph loop in CI
description: CI test output shows ralph's actual log output ('=== PHASE 2: EXECUTION ===', 'All tasks complete\!', 'Stop file detected'). Unit tests are somehow triggering the full ralph orchestrator instead of testing functions in isolation. This is dangerous — ralph could modify the CI environment, create worktrees, push to remote. Tests must be pure unit tests that never launch the full loop with real git repos or real Claude processes. Find and fix the test that calls main() or runs the full loop without proper stubbing.
close_reason: Made Config.Runner required in loop.New() — tests must inject a stub, production passes real claude.Runner. PR #109.

title: Orchestrator runs full test suite as sole verification gate
description: Remove bd close from the agent's responsibilities entirely. The agent does work, runs tests, and signals completion. The orchestrator then: (1) runs tests independently to verify, (2) if pass → orchestrator closes bead with PR number, merges PR, (3) if fail → orchestrator feeds failure back to agent for retry, agent does NOT re-signal until fixed. Remove 'close the task in bd' from execution-bd.md. Remove bd close from allowedTools if possible. The orchestrator is the only thing that closes beads — false closes become structurally impossible.
notes:
THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF ALL FALSE CLOSES. Every false close today was caused by Claude running bd close before verification. Once ralph owns the close lifecycle, false closes are structurally impossible. This must be the first P0 after ralph-c7b.
The prompt fix IS in the binary and IS being delivered to the agent. The agent is ignoring the mandatory completion order. The prompt alone is insufficient — may need programmatic enforcement: ralph detects if bead was closed before signal, and if so, reopens it. Or: remove bd close from the agent's allowed tools entirely and have ralph close after signal.
Test responsibility split: the agent runs individual/package tests during development to check its own work. The orchestrator runs the full test suite as the completion gate. The agent should NOT run the full suite as its final step — that's the orchestrator's job. This removes the 'run full test suite before signaling' instruction from the execution prompt. The agent signals when it believes it's done, the orchestrator verifies.
The orchestrator runs the full suite before handing off to the agent and tells it the result. If all pass: 'all tests passing as of start.' If some fail: 'these tests are failing, fix them before your task.' The agent never runs the full suite itself — only targeted tests during development.
Persist test results across restarts/evolve via .ralph/last-test-result.json — pass/fail, timestamp, failure output. Orchestrator writes after running suite, reads on next startup. No context accumulation — just one file overwritten each time. Evolve-compatible since .ralph/ persists across exec.
Correction: persist test results in state.json, not a separate file. state.json already holds all cross-iteration state. Add last_test_result (pass/fail), last_test_output (failure details if any), last_test_time fields.
No coverage checks in the orchestrator gate. Coverage targets lead to bullshit tests. The orchestrator checks pass/fail only. Test quality (do tests prove user-facing behavior?) is a ralph review concern, not a gate concern.
Additional orchestrator verification (all shell commands, no LLM, zero context): (1) git diff --stat — did files actually change? (2) git log origin/main..HEAD — are there new commits? (3) check bead is still in_progress, not prematurely closed by agent (4) verify PR was created and points to correct branch. These are cheap checks that catch obvious failures before running the full test suite.
When implemented: remove 'Run the full test suite at the START of your iteration' from execution-bd.md. The orchestrator tells the agent the test state on handoff. The agent runs targeted package tests during development only. The orchestrator runs the full suite as the sole gate.
The execution prompt must explicitly tell the agent: 'Do NOT run the full test suite (go test ./...). Only run tests for packages you modified (e.g. go test ./internal/git/). The orchestrator runs the full suite — you don't need to.' Without this, the agent defaults to running the full suite, wasting time and duplicating the orchestrator's job.
close_reason: bd close removed from agent via --disallowedTools. Orchestrator CloseTask implemented in PR #118. Remaining work split to new beads.

title: Fresh named branch from origin/main per task
description: Each task gets its own branch named after the bead: ralph/{project}/{NN}-{slug} (e.g. ralph/ralph/03-fix-tail-leak). Branch is created from origin/main at task start. Remove /next as a branch concept — every branch is named. The worktree stays the same, only the branch changes between tasks.
close_reason: Reordering

title: Force-reset worktree to origin/main after every squash-merge
description: After squash-merge succeeds, force-reset the worktree branch to origin/main. Create a fresh named branch for the next task. No rebasing. The old branch is disposable — its commits are on main via squash. This replaces PostMergeReset with a simpler, unconditional reset.
close_reason: Reordering — recreating as first in chain

title: Remove --auto-merge flag — merge is always on
description: Auto-merge is the only workflow. Remove: --auto-merge CLI flag, AutoMerge config field, all 'if cfg.AutoMerge' conditionals. The push/PR/squash-merge flow runs after every task completion unconditionally. Error on startup if gh CLI is not available or repo has no remote.
close_reason: Reordering — force-reset must come first

title: Remove --branch-strategy flag and BranchSingle code paths
description: Remove: --branch-strategy CLI flag, BranchStrategy config field, BranchSingle constant, all conditional logic that checks branch strategy. One workflow only. Silently ignore stale branch_strategy values in state.json and ralph.toml for evolve compatibility.

title: [bug] Ralph falsely closes beads without verifying fixes
description: Ralph repeatedly closes beads claiming fixes that don't work. The push failure (ralph-zmq) was closed while push is still failing. Multiple P0/P1 bugs were closed in a single run without any being actually fixed. The execution prompt says to verify but Claude ignores it. Possible fixes: (1) ralph should run a verification step after closing — check if the specific behavior changed, (2) ralph should not be able to close P0/P1 beads without tests proving the fix, (3) the task manager (ralph-46w) should audit closes. This is the highest-impact reliability issue in ralph.
close_reason: Root cause identified: ralph-4tt. Claude was closing beads before verification. Fix is ralph owning the close lifecycle.

title: [bug] Orphaned tail processes accumulate — stream output multiplied
description: Duplicate output from goroutine accumulation, not orphaned external processes. The Go runner's filterStreamJSON and tailGoroutine start new instances for each Run() call (main agent + verification agent), but old goroutines aren't fully stopped before new ones start. Multiple writer goroutines on loop.log produce duplicated lines. Fix: ensure filterStop/tailStop channels are properly closed and goroutines drained before any new Run() call, including verification agent runs within OnSignal.
notes:
Bash ralph handles this correctly in run_claude (ralph.sh lines 962-1072): tail_pid and filter_pid are tracked as locals, then explicitly killed with pkill -P (kill children) + kill + wait at the end of every run_claude call. Each iteration cleans up its own processes before returning. The Go version must do the same — kill tail and stream filter processes at the end of each Run() call, not just on final cleanup.
Still accumulating — 15 orphaned tail processes after a few hours of running. This makes the log output completely unreadable. The fix in PR #107 didn't work. Must kill tail and stream filter processes at the end of each Run() call, matching bash ralph's cleanup pattern (lines 1064-1072 of ralph.sh).
Evolve restart (exec) orphans child processes (tail, stream-filter). exec replaces the process but children aren't killed — they become orphans. The cleanup before exec needs to kill all child processes first. Or use process groups (setpgid) so the entire group can be killed.
close_reason: PR #131 merged — Runner-level goroutine lifecycle with StopStreaming() prevents accumulation. Verified: only correct number of file descriptors on loop.log. Kept reopening due to ralph-kduw loop on already-completed work.

title: [bug] Push fails after auto-merge deletes remote branch
description: With single-branch strategy, ralph reuses ralph/project/next for all tasks. But auto-merge passes --delete-branch to gh pr merge, which deletes the remote branch after squash. The next task's push fails because the remote branch is gone. Fix: either (1) don't pass --delete-branch in single-branch mode since the branch will be reused, or (2) after PostMergeReset, push with -u to recreate the remote branch. Option 1 is simpler. This is specific to single-branch — stacked mode creates a new branch per task so deletion is expected.
notes: Confirmed: ralph passes --delete-branch on line 414 of git.go. GitHub repo setting is false — it's ralph doing the deletion. For single-branch mode, remove --delete-branch from the gh pr merge command since the branch is reused.
close_reason: Omit --delete-branch from gh pr merge in single-branch mode. Extracted ghMergeArgs helper that conditionally includes --delete-branch only for stacked strategy. Also removed --delete-branch from shell auto_merge_current_branch.

title: Handle CI-gated repos in auto-merge
description: When auto-merge fails due to CI checks, ralph just moves on to the next task. It must: (1) after pushing PR, poll gh pr checks until CI completes, (2) if CI passes → merge, (3) if CI fails → read the failure output, fix the issue in the same iteration (not a new one), push again, wait for CI again. Loop until CI passes. The local test suite passing is not sufficient — CI may have different environments (Linux vs macOS). Ralph must treat CI as the final gate, not local tests.
notes:
Tabi requires a 'test' CI check. Ralph should: (1) run tests locally before pushing if test command is discoverable, (2) after pushing, wait for CI and check status via gh pr checks, (3) if CI fails, feed failure back to next iteration. Also consider adding --admin flag to gh pr merge for repos where the user is admin and wants to bypass checks.
Also handle merge conflicts on PRs, not just CI gates. When auto-merge fails due to conflicts, the agent should rebase onto main, resolve conflicts (it has code context), force-push, and retry merge. Currently ralph just logs the failure and moves on, leaving stacked conflicting PRs.
close_reason: completed by ralph — PR #135 merged

title: [bug] Worktree doesn't pull latest main on resume
description: When ralph resumes in an existing worktree, it should rebase onto the latest origin/main. The user synced local main with remote before running ralph, but the worktree still had stale commits. The rebase step exists but may be using local main (which was stale) instead of fetching origin/main first. Verify the resume path does: (1) git fetch origin main, (2) rebase worktree onto origin/main. This is the root cause of the 'merge commit cannot be cleanly created' failures.
close_reason: Fixed: added explicit git fetch origin/main in tryResumeWorktree (Go) and setup_worktree resume path (shell). Also switched RebaseOntoDefaultBranch fetch from gitCmd to gitCmdErr so failures are logged. Added test proving refs are updated on resume.

title: [bug] Ctrl-C does not stop Ralph in tmux mode
description: Pressing Ctrl-C in tmux mode has no effect — produces ^C characters but does not stop Ralph or kill Claude. The user has to close the terminal and manually kill orphaned processes/tmux sessions. This is the highest-friction issue in daily usage. The signal handler must: (1) catch SIGINT on first press, (2) kill the Claude child process, (3) clean up state, (4) kill the tmux session, (5) exit. In tmux mode, the signal may be going to the wrong process group. Investigate whether the Go binary needs to use process groups or setsid for proper signal delivery. Affects both bash and Go versions but Go is primary.
notes:
This was previously tracked as ralph-anv. Ralph itself claimed to fix it and closed the bead, but the fix clearly didn't work — Ctrl-C still has no effect in tmux mode. The previous close reason is unknown (bead was lost). When ralph picks this up, it must actually verify Ctrl-C works in a real tmux session before closing.
THIS BUG HAS BEEN FALSELY CLOSED THREE TIMES. Each time ralph claimed to fix it via context threading or signal handling changes, but Ctrl-C still does not work in tmux. The fix MUST be verified by actually running ralph in tmux mode and pressing Ctrl-C. Do not close based on code review alone.
Additional issue: the interactive rebase recovery prompt (promptRebaseRecovery) uses fmt.Scanln which blocks and ignores Ctrl-C. The user gets stuck at 'Choice [1/2/3]:' with no way to exit. The prompt needs to handle SIGINT or use a context-aware reader.
close_reason: Verified: Ctrl-C message shows and ralph exits gracefully. Works from any point in lifecycle — tested during setup, rebase, and execution. User confirmed.

title: [bug] Go: Auto-merge not firing — multiple tasks stacking on single branch
description: Both branch strategies (single and stacked) must share the same completion path: (1) create PR for the task's commits, (2) push and open the PR. If --auto-merge: (3) squash-merge into remote main, (4) pull to local main, (5) rebase/reset worktree to latest main for next task. This is the same flow regardless of whether commits are on a shared branch or a per-task branch. The difference between strategies is only how branches are named and rotated, not the PR/merge lifecycle. Currently single-branch skips PR creation and auto-merge between tasks, stacking everything into one PR.
notes: Gate: PR creation and auto-merge must only proceed if all tests pass. This is a hard prerequisite — no PR should be created or merged with failing tests. Run full test suite after task completion, before the PR/merge flow.
close_reason: Fixed auto-merge for both branch strategies: PostMergeReset resets worktree to origin/main after each squash-merge, PushAndCreatePR ensures Go loop owns push/PR lifecycle rather than delegating to Claude, signal-gated flow fires push/PR on completion and auto-merge when enabled. PR #97.

title: Evolve mode: verify and fix --auto-improve end-to-end
description: Evolve (--auto-improve) exists but has known issues: (1) was wiping .ralph state on restart — fixed but needs test, (2) untested end-to-end: merge → pull → rebuild → exec cycle. Verify the full cycle works: task completes, PR merged, main pulled, binary rebuilt, ralph exec's itself and resumes execution (not planning). Add integration tests. Do NOT rename the flag — that is tracked separately in ralph-al6.
notes:
Implementation: use Unix exec syscall to replace the current ralph process with the rebuilt binary. exec preserves PID, stdin/stdout/stderr, and terminal attachment — the screen stays alive and output continues seamlessly from the new binary. This is why --evolve is incompatible with --tmux: ralph creates the tmux session, so exec'ing would lose tmux management. Without tmux, ralph is just a process in the terminal and exec works cleanly. Future: tmux support would require splitting into a supervisor process that manages tmux and an inner process that does work.
Guard: --evolve must verify the project is the ralph repo itself (e.g. check for go/cmd/ralph/ or ralph.sh). Error with a clear message if used on a non-ralph project — evolve only makes sense when ralph is iterating on its own code.
Bug: autoImproveRestart calls safeRemoveRalphDir which clears .ralph state. The new process starts fresh and enters interactive planning instead of resuming execution. Fix: do NOT clear .ralph on evolve restart — state must persist so it resumes where it left off. Only clear signal files between iterations, not the entire state directory.
IMPORTANT: Split out the flag rename from --auto-improve to --evolve as the LAST subtask. The user is actively running ralph with --auto-improve. Renaming the flag mid-run would break the current session. Do all other fixes first, rename last.
close_reason: Renamed --auto-improve to --evolve throughout codebase, added ralph repo guard (checks go/cmd/ralph/), added tests for guard and state preservation, fixed pre-existing IdleTimeoutProgress test default. All 17 test packages pass.

title: Simplify to one branch strategy: fresh branch from origin/main per task
description: REMOVE all branch strategy configuration. One opinionated workflow: (1) fresh branch from origin/main per task, (2) work + commit, (3) tests pass → push + create PR + squash-merge, (4) force-reset worktree to origin/main, (5) next task. Remove: --branch-strategy flag, --auto-merge flag (merge is always on), BranchStrategy config field, BranchSingle constant, all single-branch code paths, branch_strategy from ralph.toml. Auto-merge is the default and only behavior. Evolve compatibility: silently ignore stale branch_strategy and auto_merge values in state.json/ralph.toml.
notes:

title: [bug] Single-branch stacks all tasks into one PR when merge fails

Fix: even when auto-merge fails, ralph must still create a NEW PR for the next task. Options: (1) create a new branch per task even in single-branch mode (effectively becoming stacked), (2) after failed merge, reset to main and cherry-pick only the new task's commits, (3) force-create a new PR by renaming the branch. This is distinct from ralph-8iu (rebase conflicts on resume) — this is about task isolation within a run.

title: Feed forward reflections and attempt history between tasks
description: Always feed the previous task's reflection to the next task, regardless of whether it's the same bead or a retry. Currently reflections are keyed by bead ID and only read on same-bead retries — which almost never happens because the agent rarely signals failure (it false-closes instead). Feed forward the 'what went wrong' and 'what could have gone better' sections from the last N reflections (e.g. last 3) to every new task. Universal learnings like 'run rebuild-go.sh before tests in worktrees' benefit all tasks, not just retries.
notes:
When a task is killed due to idle timeout, the next iteration must receive context about what happened: which task was being worked on, that it was killed for idle timeout (no output for 5m), and guidance to consider a lighter approach or make incremental progress rather than deep-thinking without output. This should be part of the attempt history fed forward — not just failures, but timeouts too.
Generalize: any analyzer action that kills/halts a task (idle timeout, stuck loop, stagnation, permission denial, repeated error) should write the reason into the attempt history. The next iteration receives: task ID, what was attempted, how it was killed, and the analyzer's reason. This lets Claude adjust its approach — e.g. avoid the same stuck pattern, use a different strategy, or break the work into smaller steps.

title: ralph task — interactive task manager mode
description: Standalone subcommand: 'ralph task' launches Claude interactively with a task management prompt. NOT the execution loop. Separate code path: (1) print 'Task management mode', (2) inject beads context (open beads, recently closed, project state), (3) launch Claude interactively with prompts/task-manager.md, (4) exit cleanly when Claude exits — no worktree, no iteration loop, no planning phase. Two modes: light triage (default — quick bead CRUD, concise) and hands-on fix (when explicitly asked or blocking). Handles screenshots by describing visuals and saving to .ralph/screenshots/{bead-id}-{NN}-{slug}.png. Echoes back created beads for user review. Must use bd commands correctly: create with --deps, state what changed on updates, create dependencies programmatically not in notes.
notes:
Learning: never combine 'do X now' and 'consider Y later' in the same bead. These must be separate beads with a dependency. A multi-phase task gets closed when phase 1 is done, losing the future phases. Instead: create one bead per phase, link with --deps. The task manager prompt must enforce this — if the user describes a multi-phase approach, split it into separate beads immediately.
Learnings from live tabi task management session (2026-03-22):

**Status-check before bead updates**: Before updating any bead, check if it's closed. If it was falsely closed (no evidence the described work exists or doesn't match spec), reopen it, state why it was falsely closed, and define acceptance criteria for properly closing it. If legitimately closed and user is asking for new/different work, create a new bead. Use best judgement — don't prompt the user.

**Accumulate across messages, deduplicate across beads**: When user adds details to a feature they mentioned earlier, find the existing open bead and append rather than creating a new one. Scan for duplicates before creating.

**Priority inference defaults**: Infer from context — don't ask every time. Bugs are inherently higher priority than features at the same level.
- P0: Blocking — ralph can't run, build broken, critical path completely blocked
- P1: Broken functionality (bugs), broken UX
- P2: Non-critical bugs, missing features the user explicitly asked for
- P3: Nice-to-haves, research, polish, feature requests without urgency

**Audit mode**: A way to verify recently closed beads — check if described functionality actually exists and matches spec, report mismatches. Reopen false closes with acceptance criteria stating what needs to be true to properly close.

**Two-way sync awareness with ralph loop**: Task manager should know loop is running in parallel. When creating P1 bugs, note that loop may pick them up. When the user says 'fix this now', the task manager handles it directly in hands-on fix mode rather than waiting for loop.
CRITICAL: the task manager must NEVER start ralph loop, run ralph commands, or launch nested terminal processes. It manages beads only. Starting ralph from within the task manager would create invisible nested terminals. The task manager prompt must explicitly forbid this.
Must integrate with bd states (ralph-sh2): the task manager should be able to query task states (bd state ralph-xxx), challenge closes that skipped the verified phase, and set states manually when triaging (e.g. marking a falsely-closed task as phase=unverified when reopening).

title: ralph review — post-mortem mode to integrate reflection learnings
description: ralph review mode reads reflections and performs a code health audit. Four responsibilities: (1) Read all reflections, extract patterns and recurring issues, identify learnings that should be permanent (added to AGENTS.md or prompts). (2) Audit tests: identify stale tests, tests that don't prove real user functionality (e.g. assert true), tests that pin prompt prose instead of behavior. (3) Identify refactor opportunities: files over 500 lines, dead code, naming issues, duplicated logic — using the refactor-style.md commandments. (4) Present findings to the user interactively, creating beads for approved actions. This is an interactive session like ralph task, not an autonomous loop.

title: Store screenshots for visual bugs in .ralph/screenshots/
description: When the task manager receives a screenshot for a visual bug, save it to .ralph/screenshots/{bead-id}-{NN}-{slug}.png (e.g. tabi-e2b-01-wrong-license-copy.png, tabi-e2b-02-settings-panel.png) with zero-padded two-digit numbering for sort order. The slug is a short kebab-case summary of what the screenshot shows. Multiple screenshots per bead are numbered sequentially. The agent picking up the task can read the images via Claude's multimodal Read tool to see the actual visual issue. The task manager should also include a text description alongside each path. Screenshots dir should be gitignored.

title: Task manager: echo back created bead for user review
description: After creating a bead, ralph task should echo back the ID, priority, type, title, and full description so the user can review and amend before moving on. E.g. show the bead summary and ask 'Looks good? (enter to confirm, or type changes)'. Currently the user has to run bd show to verify what was created. Short descriptions show in full, long ones truncated with option to expand.

title: Show reflection summary in log output
description: After writing a reflection, ralph just logs 'Writing reflection'. Show the first line or a truncated summary of the reflection content so the user can see what was learned without opening the file. E.g. 'Reflection: Fixed is-ancestor arg order — was comparing HEAD to main instead of main to HEAD'.

title: Install script with homebrew dependencies for Go ralph
description: Create an install script for Go ralph that handles all dependencies. Homebrew installs: bd (beads), gh (GitHub CLI). Go toolchain for building from source. No longer needs: jq (Go uses encoding/json), bash-specific tools. The install script should: (1) check/install homebrew deps, (2) clone from agent-skeleton template if new, (3) build the Go binary, (4) symlink or copy to ~/.local/bin/ralph, (5) run scripts/setup-hooks.sh. This is for when Go ralph fully replaces bash ralph and becomes the sole implementation.

title: ralph command — four-pane tmux with loop + task manager
description: 'ralph command' launches the full four-pane tmux layout: top-left is ralph loop, bottom-left is ralph task (interactive task manager), top-right is stream, bottom-right is plan. Implies --tmux. 'ralph loop' and 'ralph task' can also run standalone without tmux. 'ralph command' is the recommended way to run ralph — full visibility and control. All flags (--auto-merge, --evolve, --wait, etc.) pass through to the loop pane. The task manager pane stays alive independently for the user to interact with while the loop runs.
notes:
Tmux layout: split pane 0 (ralph) horizontally. Top-left: ralph loop output. Bottom-left: ralph task interactive session. Right side (stream + plan) unchanged. Launch both together with 'ralph --tmux' which starts the loop in top-left and task manager in bottom-left. The task manager pane stays alive independently — user can interact with it while the loop runs.
'ralph commander' launches the full four-pane tmux layout with both loop and task manager. 'ralph loop' and 'ralph task' can also run standalone.
The task manager prompt should set expectations for speed: quick triage, concise responses, create/update beads and move on. Do not deep-dive into code, explore the codebase, or attempt fixes unless explicitly asked. The user is reporting issues in real-time while ralph loop runs — the task manager needs to keep up, not block on research. Light task management, not engineering.
Two operating modes: (1) Light triage (default): quick bead creation, updates, audits. Concise responses, don't explore code unless asked. (2) Hands-on fix: when the user explicitly asks to fix something now, or when an issue blocks ralph loop from running at all. In this mode, read code, make fixes, run tests, commit. The prompt should make the default mode clear but not prevent switching to fix mode when needed.
Current state: 'ralph task' subcommand exists but is wired to the normal planning/execution flow. It needs a completely separate code path: (1) print 'Task management mode', (2) launch Claude interactively with prompts/task-manager.md, (3) exit cleanly when Claude exits — no execution phase, no worktree, no iteration loop. Currently broken — shows Phase 1 planning and falls into execution.
When the user provides screenshots, the task manager should describe what it sees and include that description in the bead. Do not store screenshots in beads — they're text-based. Note the screenshot path in the bead if needed for reproduction. The task manager prompt should instruct Claude to verbally describe visual issues from screenshots.
Depends on ralph-aus (ralph task) being complete first. ralph command integrates ralph loop + ralph task into a four-pane tmux layout — it can't work until both modes exist independently.
Learnings from live tabi task management session (2026-03-22):

**Echo back every bead creation with full description**: User needs to see exactly what was captured. Show ID, priority, type, title, and full description after every create/update. Don't make them run bd show. (See ralph-xbs.)

**Always check issue status before updating**: Never update a closed issue — create a new one or reopen first. The task manager hit this repeatedly: piling requirements onto tabi-1es which was already closed by a merged PR.

**Verify closed issues aren't falsely closed by ralph loop**: Ralph loop auto-closes beads after writing code, but the code may not match the spec. Task manager should have an audit mode: pull closed issues, verify against codebase, reopen mismatches. We had to reopen 13 issues in one session.

**Screenshot handling**: User pastes DOM + screenshot. Task manager describes the visual issue in the bead description since beads are text-only. Include site URL. For DOM problem mode bugs, follow the AGENTS.md DOM PROBLEM MODE flow (simplified DOM, verify understanding, TDD test, fix).

**Accumulate related requirements on one bead**: User often adds details to a feature across multiple messages. Task manager should update the existing open bead rather than creating duplicates. But NEVER update closed ones.

**Smart priority inference**: P1 for broken functionality, P2 for missing features and UX issues, P3 for nice-to-haves and research. User shouldn't have to specify priority every time.

**Cross-project awareness**: Task manager should know which project it's in (from cwd) and use the right bd database. When user references other projects (e.g. Ralph issues from tabi context), use --db flag.

**Hands-on fix mode**: When user says 'fix this now', switch from triage to engineering. Read code, make the fix, run tests, commit, push. Then switch back to triage mode. The keybinding fix (B=batch, M=marks) was done this way mid-session.

**Don't create bd issues for things already in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md**: These are static instructions, not tasks. Only create beads for work that needs doing.
RETRACTION: 'Cross-project awareness' note above is wrong. Task manager should be fully isolated to its project directory. No --db flag usage, no reaching into other project databases. The user (human) bridges across projects, not the agent.
close_reason: Recreating with proper dependency on ralph task

title: Rename /next branch to thematic name after planning
description: After the worktree is created, rename the /next branch to reflect the task being worked on (e.g. ralph/ralph/03-fix-tail-leak). Each task gets a descriptively named branch. The branch name comes from slugifying the bead title. On force-reset after merge, the new branch for the next task gets its own name.

title: Monitor for stuck sessions from missing allowedTools
description: IterationAllowedTools replaces --dangerously-skip-permissions. If Claude tries a tool not on the list, it blocks waiting for user approval that never comes. Add idle timeout detection for this case specifically — if Claude produces no output and no tool calls for the idle timeout period, it may be blocked on a permission prompt. Log which tool was attempted if possible. Keep the allowedTools list updated as Claude Code adds new tools.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #105: Added permission-block detection — when idle timeout fires, scans raw log for the last tool_use event, checks it against IterationAllowedTools, and logs the specific blocked tool with targeted attempt feedback. Also added TaskOutput and TaskStop to the allowed tools list.

title: Auto-name tmux session after project directory
description: Default the tmux session name to {project_dir_basename}-loop, e.g. tabi-loop, ralph-loop. Makes multiple concurrent ralph sessions distinguishable in tmux ls. Currently uses a generic name with PID. Related to ralph-4mi (thematic worktree naming).
close_reason: Implemented project-based tmux session naming ({basename}-loop) in both Go and shell codepaths, with sanitization and collision avoidance. PR #101.

title: Truncate task title in stream pane to reasonable length
description: Stream pane title shows the full bead title which can be very long (e.g. '[bug] Go: Auto-merge not firing — multiple tasks stacking on single branch'). Truncate to ~50-60 chars with ellipsis so the elapsed time is always visible. Format: 'ralph-9uu: Auto-merge not firing — multi... 3m05s'. The bead ID + truncated title + elapsed time should always fit in the pane border.
close_reason: Added truncateTask helper in panetitle.go that caps task+elapsed to 60 chars with ellipsis. Title() applies truncation; Task() still returns full label. Tests cover both long and short titles.

title: Wait mode: keep ralph alive polling for new tasks
description: Add --wait flag that keeps ralph running after all tasks complete. Instead of exiting, it polls bd ready on an interval (e.g. every 30s) and picks up new tasks as they appear. Works in both tmux and inline modes. The user creates tasks from another terminal (bd create) and ralph picks them up automatically. In tmux, keep the three-pane layout alive with 'Waiting for tasks...' in the ralph pane and plan pane updated. In inline mode, log the waiting status. Ctrl-C or ralph stop exits as normal.
close_reason: Added --wait flag and --wait-interval to config, loop, and CLI. Loop polls task backend at configurable interval when all tasks complete, resuming on new tasks. Stop file and Ctrl-C exit cleanly. 4 loop tests + 3 config tests added. PR #102.

title: Bump patch version on each merged PR
description: Each PR merged into main increments the patch version automatically. Ralph only does patch bumps on auto-merge — minor and major bumps are manual/user-decided. Use Go ldflags to inject version at build time. Git tags as source of truth — ralph creates a patch tag after auto-merge. rebuild-go.sh reads the latest tag and passes it via ldflags.
close_reason: Fixed BumpPatchTag to tag specific ref (origin/main) instead of HEAD, switched LatestVersionTag to global tag search, added GH Action dedup guard. PR #103.

title: Confusing branch name shown at startup before rebase
description: When resuming, the ralph pane shows the old worktree branch name from the previous run (e.g. '02-bug-go-stream-pane-title') before it rebases and renames to the current task. The stream pane then shows the actual current task. This makes it look like Ralph is working on two different things. Either suppress the old branch name, or show it as 'Resuming from: ...' to make it clear it's transitional.
close_reason: Fixed: on resume, .run-branch now shows 'resuming…' instead of stale old task branch name. Updated both shell (ralph.sh) and Go (main.go + loop.go) paths. Branch label updates to real name once the first iteration renames it.

title: Show [MERGED] status next to branches in exit summary
description: When Ralph exits and lists all branches it created, each branch should show whether it has been merged into main. Display [MERGED] in capitals after branches that were squash-merged. With --auto-merge, all branches except possibly the last (if interrupted) would show [MERGED]. Helps the user know which branches are safe to delete and which have pending work.

title: Show completed tasks in plan pane
description: After the 'X/Y done' line in the plan pane, show recently completed task IDs in a comma-separated list on one line. E.g. '12/15 done' followed by 'ralph-abc, ralph-def, ralph-ghi'. Saves vertical space versus listing each completed task on its own line. Only show completions from the current run, not all historical closures.

title: Go: Clean up orphaned worktrees on startup
description: Orphaned worktrees from previous agent runs or crashed ralph sessions accumulate in .ralph/worktrees/ and .claude/worktrees/. On startup, detect and prune worktrees whose branches no longer exist or whose directories are stale. Use 'git worktree prune' and optionally remove directories that aren't associated with any active branch.

title: Go: Refactor iteration config flags and disable option
description: Add CLI flags and config file options for tuning refactor behavior: quality score threshold, which checks to enable/disable, and a flag to disable refactoring entirely (e.g. --no-refactor). Currently the quality threshold and checks are hardcoded.

description: The version string shows 'v0.1.0 (go)' vs 'v0.1.0' but this is easy to miss. Make the distinction more prominent — e.g. in the tmux session name, pane title, or a clear startup banner. The user needs to know at a glance which binary is running.

title: Add --plan flag to force re-entry into planning mode
description: There's no way to enter planning mode when beads already exist. The user may want to review, reprioritize, or add tasks before resuming execution. Add a --plan flag that enters interactive planning regardless of whether tasks exist. The planning prompt should show existing beads as context so the user and Claude can modify the plan rather than starting from scratch.

title: Clean up stale REFACTOR_EVERY references in config loader
description: The adaptive quality-based REFACTOR_THRESHOLD replaced the old REFACTOR_EVERY approach, but config file loader and CLI arg tracking still reference refactor_every. Clean up dead config paths.
close_reason: Removed all stale REFACTOR_EVERY references from shell config loader, Go config/state/loop packages, CLI flags, env var overrides, and tests. PR #86.

title: Fix auto_merge.bats hang in full test suite — EXIT trap cleanup isolation
description: When running all bats test files together, auto_merge.bats causes the suite to hang. The EXIT trap from ralph.sh fires during bash subprocess cleanup. Individual test files pass fine. The Go test runner should handle process isolation properly.
close_reason: Guarded EXIT/INT/TERM trap installation behind RALPH_SOURCED check so traps only install when ralph.sh runs as a script, not when sourced for functions. Removed workaround trap - EXIT calls from test_helper.bash and auto_merge.bats. PR #87.

title: Auto-merge PRs between iterations
description: Add a flag (e.g. --auto-merge) that squash-merges each PR into main after a task completes, before starting the next iteration. Useful for one-shotting new repos where review isn't needed between tasks. Each subsequent task's branch would be created rebased on the freshly merged main. Should be opt-in since the default workflow assumes human review between PRs.
close_reason: Added --auto-merge flag: opt-in squash-merge of each PR into main after task completion via gh CLI. Go CLI + bash + tests.

title: Simplify iteration counter display
description: The log line 'Iteration 1/50 (23 total)' is confusing — unclear which number is per-run vs cumulative. Both are useful, but the display needs to make the distinction obvious. E.g. 'Run iteration 1/50 | 23 lifetime' or similar. Keep both counters, just clarify the labels.
close_reason: Clarified iteration counter labels across Go and shell: 'Iteration X/Y (Z total)' → 'Run iteration X/Y | Z lifetime'. Updated phase lines, completion lines, and summary output.

title: Adaptive refactoring — replace fixed schedule with quality signals
description: Replace the fixed refactor_every counter with adaptive refactoring. Ralph should evaluate code quality signals after each task and decide whether a refactor iteration is warranted. The style guide (prompts/refactor-style.md) defines the commandments and bestiary of code sins — use these as the evaluation criteria. Signals to check: file size growth, type coverage degradation, silent catches, dead code accumulation, naming violations, dependency bloat. Could run a lightweight analysis pass (line counts, grep for TODOs/any/console.log, duplicate function signatures) and trigger refactoring when pain crosses a threshold rather than on a fixed cadence.

title: Go: Reset refactor counter on resume
description: iterations_since_refactor must reset to 0 at the start of run_execution, not carry over from previous runs. Reference commit and ralph.sh run_execution.
close_reason: Added ResetForExecution method to State that clears quality_score and re-applies config values at execution start, matching ralph.sh behavior

title: Name tmux sessions after worktree/task theme
description: Tmux sessions currently use a generic name. Name them after the worktree or task theme (same name used for worktree renaming) so multiple ralph sessions are distinguishable. Makes tmux ls output meaningful.
close_reason: Tmux sessions now renamed to match worktree basename after planning produces a theme. Shell and Go paths updated with tests.

title: Tmux dead-pane exit hint and key binding
description: When remain-on-exit shows dead panes, the user is trapped with no way to close the session from inside. Add a tmux hook or key binding (e.g. press q to kill session) that works on dead panes. Could use set-hook pane-died or after-display-message. Also show a hint in the pane border or status bar.
close_reason: Added dead-pane exit hint and q key binding to Go tmux session. Pane borders show '(dead) — press q to exit' via pane_dead conditional. Bound q in root key table to kill session when ralph pane 0 is dead.

title: Go: Stream pane title via shared state, not file
description: The bash implementation uses .stream-task file to pass task ID + title from the main loop to the tmux timer background process. In Go, use shared state (e.g. atomic string or mutex-protected field) instead of a file. The timer goroutine can read directly from the loop's current task state.
close_reason: Added tmux.PaneTitle type with mutex-protected shared state replacing .stream-task file. SetTask/ResetTimer for main loop, Title()/Run() for timer goroutine. PR #55.

title: Replace repeated-tool-call stuck detection with better heuristics
description: The current stuck detection counts repeated tool+target pairs per iteration (5+ triggers). This produces false positives during normal development — reading the same file 5 times in one iteration is routine. Remove this heuristic and replace with more reliable detection: (1) no git diff + no new commits + completion signal = suspicious, (2) same task picked up N consecutive iterations without progress, (3) Claude explicitly says it's blocked. Repeated tool calls across a session (not consecutive) are not meaningful — only consecutive identical calls in a tight loop indicate actual stuck behavior. The stagnation detector (no-change across iterations) already catches the real stuck case.
close_reason: Removed repeated tool call counting from Go analyzer. Only explicit stuck phrases remain. Committed on main.

title: Config file for tweakable defaults
description: Add a ralph config file (e.g. ralph.toml or .ralph.yml) in the project root that groups all tweakable constants with sensible defaults. Command-line args override config values. Constants to include: max_iterations, refactor_every, stuck_threshold (currently 5), stagnation_threshold, test_saturation_threshold, calls_per_hour, watcher_interval. Both bash and Go implementations should read from this.
close_reason: Added ralph.toml config file support with load_config() parser, --init-config subcommand, configurable analysis thresholds, env var/CLI precedence chain, and 10 bats tests. PR #57.

title: Fix Go analyzer: bump stuck threshold from 3 to 5
description: The Go port (go/internal/analyzer/) used the old threshold of 3 repeated tool calls. Bash was updated to 5 in commit 15dc019. Update the Go code to match.
close_reason: No Go port exists yet — there is no go/ directory in the repo. The bash implementation (ralph.sh) already has STUCK_THRESHOLD=5. This task was created prematurely; it will be relevant when the Go migration creates the analyzer package.

title: Persist _TASK_SEQ in state.json across resumes
description: Branch sequence numbers skip when ralph resumes because _TASK_SEQ resets to 0 on script restart while branches from previous runs still exist. Fix: persist _TASK_SEQ in state.json and restore on resume. Or scan existing branches to derive the next sequence number.
close_reason: Persisted _TASK_SEQ in state.json: stored on branch rename and post-rebase, restored on resume with fallback to branch count for backward compatibility. PR #58.

title: Idle timeout detection
description: Monitor log file modification time during claude execution. If no output for N minutes (configurable, default 10), kill session and restart iteration. Shorter timeout (30s) if progress was already made in this iteration (detected via git diff or new log lines). Integrate into claude process management goroutine.
close_reason: Implemented idle timeout detection: monitors raw log mod time, 10min default timeout, 30s shorter timeout when progress detected (git diff/commits), configurable via CLI flags and env vars. PR #64.

title: Post-task reflections saved to file
description: On successful task completion, save structured reflection to .ralph/reflections/<task_id>.md. Captures: what was discovered, what was missing from the prompt, what would help future iterations. Accumulated for human review and future prompt integration. Add reflection instructions to execution prompt templates.
close_reason: Added post-task reflection prompt template and wired it into both shell and Go prompt assembly. Claude now writes structured reflections to .ralph/reflections/<task-id>.md before signaling completion.

title: Git tags per task
description: Create ralph/task-{id}/start git tag at beginning of each task iteration. Enables per-task rollback and audit trail. Tag created after task selection, before claude runs. On task skip/complete, optionally create ralph/task-{id}/end tag.
close_reason: Added TagTaskStart/TagTaskEnd to git.Manager creating lightweight tags at ralph/task-{id}/start and ralph/task-{id}/end. Wired into execution loop before/after Claude runs. Six tests. PR #66.

title: Attempt history fed back to Claude
description: After each iteration, record what was attempted to .ralph/attempts/<task_id>.log (summary, git diff stat, analysis result). On re-attempt of same task, include history in prompt via {{ATTEMPT_HISTORY}} template variable. Clear attempt file only when task is resolved (completed or skipped-as-blocked) — must persist across --resume. Add attempt history section to prompts/internal.md.
close_reason: Implemented attempt history: records attempts to .ralph/attempts/<key>.log after each iteration, feeds history into Claude prompt via {{ATTEMPT_HISTORY}} on re-attempts, clears on task resolution. Also fixed pre-existing test failures (122/122 pass). PR #67.

title: Per-task stuck detection — skip and continue
description: Make stuck/stagnation/test-saturation detection per-task instead of global. When a task is stuck, mark it blocked (bd close --reason 'blocked: ...') and continue to next task instead of halting the entire run. Permission denial still halts globally. Reset counters on task change. Safety net: max attempts per task (default 5). Add skip_task to task backend interface.
close_reason: Implemented per-task stuck detection: halt conditions (stuck_loop, stagnation, test_saturation) now skip the task and continue instead of halting the run. Added skip_task to backend interface, per-task attempt tracking (max 5), counter reset on task change. Permission denial still halts globally. PR #70.

title: Error normalization in response analyzer
description: Extract error lines from Claude output (Error:, Failed:, Exception:, panic:, non-zero exit codes). Normalize by stripping timestamps, UUIDs, line numbers, temp paths, collapsing whitespace. MD5 fingerprint normalized errors. Track in .ralph/.error_hashes per task. Threshold: same fingerprint 3x → trigger per-task skip. Clear fingerprints on task change.
close_reason: Implemented error normalization and fingerprinting in response analyzer. Extracts error lines, normalizes by stripping volatile parts, MD5 fingerprints them, tracks per-task in .ralph/error_hashes. Same fingerprint 3x triggers halt:repeated_error and task skip. PR #71.

title: Go: Tmux session management
description: Port setup_tmux — 3-pane layout (status | claude output | plan progress). Use tmux remain-on-exit to keep all panes visible after normal exit. On Ctrl-C/interrupt, outer wrapper kills the whole session. Stream pane title shows task ID + summary with elapsed time. Plan pane shows current task + ready queue + unblocks. Reference ralph.sh tmux functions and commit 20efeab for current implementation. Creates: go/internal/tmux/

title: Spawn verification agent on second no-diff signal to check if feature exists in codebase
description:
When the agent signals completion with no PR and no diff, the current behavior (fire mode) trusts the agent and accepts. Add a configurable trust level:

- fire (default): accept agent's claim immediately, close task
- hog: spawn a verification agent to read the codebase and confirm the feature exists before closing

title: Update README with opinionated workflow and current architecture
description: After all P0-P2 work is done, update README.md to reflect: one workflow (fresh branch per task, squash-merge, force-reset), Go-only implementation, ralph loop / ralph task / ralph command subcommands, bd as the only task backend, evolve mode, auto-merge as default behavior. title: Deprecate ralph feedback in favor of ralph task + beads
description: ralph feedback injects text into the next iteration's prompt — no persistence, no tracking, no verification. It does NOT interrupt the current iteration; it's picked up on the next one. This is identical to creating a bead, which also gets picked up on the next iteration. Beads are strictly better: persistent, tracked, auditable, can be reopened, have priority. There is no use case where feedback adds value over ralph task + beads. Remove feedback entirely rather than deprecating.
close_reason: we want feedback for communication and can now do it real time instead unlike a task

title: Rename --auto-improve flag to --evolve
description: Rename the CLI flag from --auto-improve to --evolve for clarity. Must be done AFTER all other auto-improve fixes are complete since the user actively runs with --auto-improve. Update flag parsing, help text, state values, and any references.
close_reason: Renamed --auto-improve to --evolve across all Go source: CLI flag, Config.AutoImprove→Evolve, auto_improve_restart→evolve_restart state value, autoImproveRestart→evolveRestart function, log messages, help text, and all tests.

title: Filter escape sequences from stream pane output
description: Arrow key presses in tmux panes produce ^[[A/^[[B escape sequences in the stream output when the pane process (tail -f) doesn't consume them. Filter these out in the stream filter script so they don't clutter the logs. Could also set the pane to read-only or disable input forwarding for panes 1 and 2 since they're display-only.
close_reason: Added stty -echo to stream filter and plan watcher scripts (Go + shell) to suppress terminal escape sequences in display-only tmux panes. Tests added for both.

title: Review git tag naming for task start/end markers
description: Ralph creates tags like 'ralph/task-ralph-ner/start' and 'ralph/task-ralph-ner/end' to mark task boundaries. The naming is redundant (ralph appears twice) and the tags themselves may not be useful — the information is already in beads and git history. Consider removing tags entirely or simplifying to 'task/ralph-ner/start' if they serve a purpose.
close_reason: Simplified task tag naming from ralph/task-{id}/{suffix} to task/{id}/{suffix}, removing the redundant ralph prefix. Tags are kept since they provide useful task boundary markers in git history.

title: Revisit auto-merge feature after single-branch implementation
description: The auto-merge feature (ralph-67p) may be redundant once we switch from stacked branches to single worktree branch with one-shot commits. After implementing the single-branch approach, evaluate whether auto-merge is still needed or if it should be removed. The stacked branch model needed merging between tasks; a single branch may not.
close_reason: Auto-merge is still needed: stacked branches (one per task) are still used. Wired --auto-merge through Go loop (calls AutoMergeCurrentBranch after task signals) and resume script. PR #88.

title: Go: Handle squash-merge rebase failures gracefully
description: When rebase fails due to squash-merged branches, Ralph should prompt the user with options: (1) create a fresh worktree from current main (delete old worktree, clear state, keep beads), (2) manually resolve conflicts, (3) abort. Currently it just halts with an error. The fresh worktree option is almost always what the user wants since completed work is already on main via squash merge.
close_reason: Added RebaseConflictError type, RecreateFromMain method, and OnRebaseConflict handler callback. When rebase fails, the loop consults a configurable handler offering fresh worktree, manual resolve, or abort options. CLI wires up an interactive prompt. 6 new tests cover all recovery paths.

title: Tmux UI polish — low-effort high-leverage improvements
description:
Ideas for improving the tmux layout with minimal effort:
- Color the iteration counter in pane 0 (green when progressing, yellow on warn, red on halt)
- Show a progress bar in the plan pane (visual ratio of closed/total tasks)
- Show elapsed time per-run in the ralph pane title (not just per-task in stream)
- Flash/highlight the plan pane border when a task completes
- Show the worktree branch name in the ralph pane title
- Add a status line at the bottom showing rate limit remaining, calls this hour
- Dim completed tasks in the ready list instead of hiding them entirely
close_reason: Implemented 5 of 7 tmux UI improvements: progress bar in plan pane, branch+elapsed in ralph pane title, dimmed completed tasks with checkmarks, plan border flash on completion, colored iteration counter (green/yellow). All tests pass. PR #104 updated.
